# Turn a formula into a printable label

> Calculate theoretical nutrient and ingredient composition from a reviewed batch formula. Trace sources, missing data, and assumptions before using a result.

Canonical: https://formula.significanthobbies.com/

Formula calculator

Paste your formula or upload a file. Generate the printable label with the best supported estimates.

Formula input

## Start with one formula

Ingredient quantities are for
- One dose / serving

- A finished production batch

Dose volume (mL): 15

Enter amounts per dose. A dose-volume line is optional; this is not a production batch.

Paste text, a table, or JSON

```text
PAPAIN 60 MG
LYSINE 15 MG
NIACINAMIDE 3 MG
VITAMIN B1 1 MG
VITAMIN B6 .75 MG
```

Upload a file instead

Drop a formula here or choose a file Text, CSV, JSON, XLSX, PNG/JPEG/WebP/BMP, or PDF · Maximum 12 MiB

Prepare formula for review

Examples, references and activity log

[Download sample](https://formula.significanthobbies.com/sample-tonic.tsv)

Download activity log

The activity log records actions and times without formula text. On the public site, Clarity measures visits and interactions with the application content masked.

# How our results compare

> See how the formula calculator compares with published food and medicine values.

Canonical: https://formula.significanthobbies.com/case-studies/

Evidence as of: 2026-09-21

Public checks

We entered 26 public food and medicine formulas into the calculator. Below are all 55 ingredient and nutrient values that the public sources gave us enough information to check.

- 26 products

- 55 values compared

- 3 public sources

## How to read this page

Published is the value shown by WHO, USDA, or DailyMed. Calculated is our result from the product formula. Difference shows how far apart they are.

We compare every ingredient and nutrient amount supported by these checks. We do not compare acidity, tablet weight, or ingredients whose amounts were not published. We never guess a missing amount. These checks do not replace a laboratory test or show government approval.

Full results
